review_notes:
I read all 152 lines of the target file. I also read the definitions it builds on in Sheaves/Frames.lean: `endValue`, `endValue_id` (which is @[simp]), `endValue_comp`, `coefficient`, `restrictSection`, `coefficient_restrict`, `restrictSection_comp` and `coefficient_transport`. I checked `restrictSection_postcomp` in Divisors/SectionTransport.lean, which this file does not import. I also looked at downstream uses in LocalAlgebra/PowerIdeal.lean and at similar code in Geometry/GeometricDivision.lean and Divisors/CartierResidual.lean.

The main simp problem is missing coverage. Nothing in this file's imports normalises `restrictSection φ (s ≫ f)`. The only lemma that does it, `restrictSection_postcomp`, is in a module this file cannot see and has no simp attribute. As a result the same identity is proved by hand in at least five places. Two of those are in this file, and one is inside a 15-line calc that gets the whole of `affineCoefficient_iso`'s key equality by hand.

The proposed orientation, `restrictSection φ (s ≫ f) ↦ restrictSection φ s ≫ (restrictFunctor φ).map f`, follows `Functor.map_comp`. The right side has no `restrictSection` applied to a composite, so the rule cannot loop with itself. It also fits with `restrictSection_comp`, whose left side has the form `restrictSection (φ ≫ ψ) s ≫ _` with the composite in the immersion argument.

Other points I considered and did not report:
- Making `endValue_comp` simp. It is rewritten in both directions (`rw [← endValue_comp]` here and in Frames), so a fixed orientation is not clearly better.
- The `unfold affineCoefficient` and `simp only [..., affineCoefficient]` patterns. These are local and harmless.
- `associated_unit_middle`, which is a purely algebraic helper and not a simp candidate.

I could not run Lean, so the replacement proofs are untested. In particular, whether `simp` closes `equality` on its own depends on how `Iso.trans_hom`, `Functor.mapIso_hom` and `Category.assoc` interact. If it does not, a short `rw` chain using the same lemmas should work.

findings.problem: The expression `restrictSection U.1.ι (t ≫ multiplication)` has no simp rule in this file's import closure, so it is not simplified. Its natural normal form is `restrictSection U.1.ι t ≫ (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.1.ι).map multiplication`, which is what `Functor.map_comp` would give if `restrictSection` were unfolded. The rule that does this, `restrictSection_postcomp`, sits in Divisors/SectionTransport.lean, which this file does not import, and has no simp attribute. So this proof rebuilds the identity by hand from `map_comp` and `Category.assoc`. The same manual proof appears in `affineCoefficient_iso` (lines 36–47), in `affineCoefficient_map` (PowerIdeal.lean) and in GeometricDivision.lean and CartierResidual.lean.
findings.proposed_change: Move `restrictSection_postcomp` next to `restrictSection` in Sheaves/Frames.lean, unchanged except for the attribute: `@[simp] lemma restrictSection_postcomp (φ : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion φ] (s : O X ⟶ M) (f : M ⟶ N) : restrictSection φ (s ≫ f) = restrictSection φ s ≫ (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor φ).map f`. Adding `@[reassoc]` as well is optional. Then replace `restrictedComposition` with `restrictSection_postcomp U.1.ι t multiplication`, or let `simp` apply it inside the calc. Do the same for the `show ... by exact (congrArg ...)` block in `PowerIdeal.affineCoefficient_map` and for `hc` in GeometricDivision.lean.
findings.benefit: One oriented rule replaces at least five hand-built proofs of the same identity. With the rule, `simp` (and `simp [coefficient_postcompose]`) can move a postcomposed morphism out of `restrictSection` automatically. The orientation matches `Functor.map_comp`. It cannot loop, because the right side contains no `restrictSection` of a composite. Readers no longer have to parse `congrArg`/`Category.assoc` chains to see a routine functoriality step.

findings.excerpt:
have equality : affineCoefficient U (restriction.mapIso g ≪≫ f) s =
      affineCoefficient U f (s ≫ g.hom) :=
    congrArg (fun value => U.1.topIso.hom value) (congrArg endValue composition)
findings.problem: The key step needs `coefficient (restriction.mapIso g ≪≫ f) (restrictSection U.1.ι s)` and `coefficient f (restrictSection U.1.ι (s ≫ g.hom))` to have the same normal form. The library already has both halves of this. `coefficient_transport` sends `coefficient (e ≪≫ f) s` to `coefficient f (s ≫ e.hom)`. `restrictSection_postcomp` sends `restrictSection (s ≫ g.hom)` to `restrictSection s ≫ restriction.map g.hom`. But neither lemma is tagged simp, and `restrictSection_postcomp` is not even imported here. So the proof goes through the raw definitions: a 12-line `composition` calc that re-proves `map_comp` with associativity by hand, followed by `congrArg endValue`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `coefficient_transport` in Frames.lean `@[simp]`, keeping its current direction: `coefficient (e ≪≫ f) s = coefficient f (s ≫ e.hom)`. Also make `restrictSection_postcomp` (moved to Frames.lean) `@[simp]`, as in the previous finding. Then `composition` can be deleted, and `equality` can be proved by `simp only [affineCoefficient, coefficient_transport, Functor.mapIso_hom, restrictSection_postcomp]`, or by an equivalent `rw` chain. Both sides should then reduce to `U.1.topIso.hom (coefficient f (restrictSection U.1.ι s ≫ restriction.map g.hom))`.
findings.benefit: The two orientations push the frame isomorphism into the section and the postcomposed morphism out of `restrictSection`, so both sides reach the same normal form. Neither rule's right side contains the other rule's left-hand pattern, so the pair should not cycle. The proof of `affineCoefficient_iso` shrinks to its mathematical content: change of frame together with transport along `g`. Later lemmas of the same shape, such as those built on `affineCoefficient_division`, get the same automation.
